paper_title: Text Generation with Diffusion Language Models A Pre-training Approach   with Continuous Paragraph Denoise
caption: Effect of different diffusion steps on text generation quality, on XSum. The result is the optimal value of 5 Gaussian samples.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the impact of different diffusion steps on text generation quality, measured on the XSum dataset, with results representing the optimal value across 5 Gaussian samples. The horizontal axis, labeled "Diffusion Step," displays five discrete values: 100, 250, 500, 1000, and 2000. The vertical axis represents the evaluation metric, with values ranging from approximately 0.1 to 41.2. Three models are compared: ROUGE-1 (light blue, diagonal stripes), ROUGE-2 (light green, dot pattern), and ROUGE-L (orange, dot pattern). For each diffusion step, three bars are grouped together, showing the performance of each model. As the diffusion step increases, the performance of all three models generally improves. At the 100-step mark, ROUGE-1 scores 6.3, ROUGE-2 scores 0.1, and ROUGE-L scores 3.0. At 2000 steps, ROUGE-1 reaches its peak score of 41.2, ROUGE-2 scores 19.1, and ROUGE-L scores 33.4. The legend in the top-left corner identifies the models and their corresponding bar patterns.
